task.description:
REWORK RE-CHECK (your prior FAIL, handoffs/WF01-TESTPARALLEL-20260821/step-02-req-validator.json's own previous result, is preserved in git history / your own completed handoff before this re-dispatch overwrote it -- see handoffs/orchestrator.log for the full prior verdict text if needed). REQ-ANALYST's rework iteration 1 applied ORCH's provisional picks from docs/migration/decisions/0008-cross-cutting-tooling-stage-and-doc-ownership.md: REQ-113 and REQ-114 both changed stage: S0 to stage: S4, and each got a one-sentence citation of decision 0008 added to its description (REQ-113: justifying the S4 tag; REQ-114: justifying both the S4 tag and DOC-UPDATER as owner despite workflow docs not being in DOC-UPDATER's previously-documented remit). Per the rework instructions given to REQ-ANALYST, your job THIS pass is narrower than a full re-run of checks a-e: confirm (1) both stage fields now read S4, (2) both descriptions actually contain a citation of decision 0008, (3) REQ-114's owner is still DOC-UPDATER, (4) nothing else on either requirement regressed (spot-check acceptance_criteria/depends_on/title are unchanged from what you already validated as PASS on checks a/b/c/e last pass -- REQ-113 testability/consistency/depends_on/size and REQ-114 testability/depends_on/size). You are NOT expected to re-litigate whether decision 0008's picks themselves are correct -- that's REVIEWER's job at REQ-114's WF-02 Step 2d gate per the decision file's own Status line -- only whether REQ-ANALYST actually applied them faithfully and didn't break anything else in the process. If REQ-ANALYST's edit is faithful and nothing regressed: PASS. If the citation is missing, the stage/owner fields don't match, or something else broke: FAIL with specifics, same as any other validator pass.

ORIGINAL TASK (for context on what checks a-e originally covered): REQ-ANALYST just drafted REQ-113 and REQ-114 into docs/requirements.yaml (grep for '  - id: REQ-113' and '  - id: REQ-114' to find them -- do not read the whole 61k-token file). REQ-113: parallel test-runner script (scripts/test_parallel.sh) via Elixir's native --partitions flag, owner ELIXIR-DEV, stage S0, depends_on []. REQ-114: wire that script into TEST-RUNNER Step 4 / RELEASE-VALIDATOR Step 5 across the workflow docs, owner DOC-UPDATER, stage S0, depends_on [REQ-113]. Run your normal Step 2 checks against both: TESTABILITY (every acceptance criterion has a pass/fail test, no vague words), CONSISTENCY (no conflict with a done requirement or a docs/migration/decisions/*.md record), DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS, STAGE FIT, SIZE (one agent turn each, not smuggling multiple deliverables).

Two things REQ-ANALYST explicitly flagged for you to weigh in on rather than deciding unilaterally -- read its handoff's result.issues (handoffs/WF01-TESTPARALLEL-20260821/step-01-req-analyst.json) for its own reasoning, then form your own independent verdict, don't just rubber-stamp its flag:
1. Stage fit: both tagged S0 on the REQ-013 precedent (a prior non-porting, dev-pipeline-tooling item that also landed in S0), even though docs/migration/README.md describes S0 as already fully expanded (REQ-010..014) and this would be the first S0 addition since REQ-014. Decide independently whether S0 is the right tag, or whether these belong outside the S0-S8 numbering entirely (and if so, what your check c should actually require the field to contain, since the schema calls for one of S0-S8) -- state your reasoning either way.
2. REQ-114's owner is DOC-UPDATER but its task is editing workflow *process* docs (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02/03/04_*.md and possibly .claude/agents/test-runner.md, release-validator.md), not docs/requirements.yaml/docs/status/ (DOC-UPDATER's normal remit per AGENT_SYSTEM.md). Check whether DOC-UPDATER is actually the right owner for editing agent workflow/role docs, or whether this should be ELIXIR-DEV (continuing from REQ-113) or ORCH-direct (workflow docs are not lib/ or tests, and ORCH is explicitly the one who dispatches per those docs -- though core-directives.md's sizing rule may still require the full pipeline given it changes a gate TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR depend on).

If either requirement fails any check, FAIL with the specific requirement id and check letter -- do not fix it yourself, that goes back to REQ-ANALYST as rework.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-e (testability, consistency, depends_on correctness, stage fit, size) were actually run against BOTH REQ-113 and REQ-114's real text, not assumed
The stage-fit question and the REQ-114 owner question above were both independently re-derived, not copied from REQ-ANALYST's own flag
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and which check failed, precisely enough for REQ-ANALYST to fix without re-reading this whole handoff
